text: Abigail gripped the polished mahogany handrail of the luxury liner as it cut through the choppy waters of the Pacific, heading toward the bustling ports of San Francisco. It was 1924, and she was leaving behind the rigid social expectations of her upper-class life in London for the promise of jazz, freedom, and reinvention in the United States. She clutched her small, leather-bound vanity case that contained all her worldly possessions, her heart racing with both fear and excitement. Tell me what a book is primarily made of.
